title: KV access burst saturation playbook
content:
TL;DR:
This note documents investigation steps, quick experiments, and mitigations for a recurring failure mode: short, high-QPS bursts saturating memory bandwidth and causing elevated KV cache eviction + paging, which inflates tail latency for small-text generation requests. Goal is a reproducible playbook to detect, reproduce, and mitigate with config/patches.

Background / Why this matters:
- Production symptom: sudden 5–20s bursts of requests (from client-side retries/PLG onboarding flows) produce a spike in page faults and device-to-host DMA, KV residency drops ~30–60% for hot keys, and 99th latency doubles.
- These bursts are not steady-state and often slip past existing autoscaling and batching heuristics because they are short-duration.
- Root suspected: a combination of long-tailed access patterns that cross NUMA boundaries, large per-request KV scans when warmup misses occur, and memory bandwidth contention causing increased latency to fetch KV pages (and fallback eviction).

Observed signals (recent incident 2025-11-12):
- 1-min QPS spike: 6x baseline for ~12s.
- Kernel / VM stats: soft page faults increased 8x, dmesg showed occasional DMA-stall warnings on NIC->GPU host paths.
- Memory bandwidth (perf counters): sustained 45–70% higher DRAM reads vs baseline.
- KV metrics: hot-key reuse rate fell from 92% to 61% for the median shard; eviction rate increased 3x; cache hit latency median increased 30us -> 120us.
- Scheduling/NIC: small correlation with co-located batch jobs on same host; NUMA node bounce seen in page ownership graphs.

Repro recipe (dev cluster):
1) Dataset: small-model request traces with heavy token short responses (prompt -> 8–12 tokens). Use trace tool: reproduce_trace.py --sample=burst_short_texts --qps_profile=spike12s.json
2) Run target binary with perf counters: sudo perf stat -e L1-dcache-load-misses,mem_load_uops_retired.l3_miss,dram_read_bytes -p $(pidof serving-runtime) -- sleep 30
3) Attach eBPF hotspot script to record kv-page faults and page migration events (kv-pagewatcher.rb).
4) Measure KV residency: curl -s http://localhost:9000/metrics | grep kv_residency | tee residency.out
5) Toggle NUMA binding for worker threads: taskset -c <numa-cpu-list> and compare.

Empirical quick experiments and outcomes:
- Locality pinning: binding serving threads and GPU DMA threadlets to the same NUMA node reduced burst-induced page migrations by ~45% and kept eviction increase to 1.2x instead of 3x.
- Micro-batching window increase: increasing the small-request micro-batch window from 2ms -> 6ms reduced total DRAM read amplification and improved 99p latency during bursts by ~18% but increased median by ~5%. Tradeoff worth for tail SLOs in many workloads.
- Aggressive prefetching of predicted next keys (prefetch 2 ahead when reuse probability > 0.6) helped when reuse patterns were sequential; in highly random access it wasted bandwidth and worsened latencies. So enable via runtime adaptive heuristic only.
- Reduced eviction aggressiveness (extend TTL for recently-resident pages) lowered thrashing in tests with repeaters but increased memory pressure long-term. Good for short bursts but requires a fallback.
- Page size experiment: promoting hot segments to 2MB hugepages reduced per-page metadata churn but made eviction granularity coarser; overall improved bandwidth efficiency for heavy bursts in our traces.

Profiling artifacts to collect for next incident triage (template):
- QPS timeline (1s resolution) + client request size distribution.
- perf counters (DRAM read/write bytes, last-level cache miss rate) with 5s windows.
- KV metrics: per-shard hit/miss/evict/residency, per-key reuse histogram (5ms bin).
- eBPF traces of page faults + migrate events.
- NUMA page ownership snapshot.
Store artifacts in GH artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-profiles/INF-2143/<timestamp>/

Short-term mitigations (config + quick deployable):
1) Enable NUMA-aware worker scheduling by default in dedicated pools (config flag: numa_worker_affinity=true).
2) Increase micro-batch coalescing window for small token responses to 5–8ms behind a per-route knob.
3) Adaptive prefetch: in-flight heuristic gate + per-route enable flag (off by default for random access workloads).
4) Eviction hysteresis: if eviction rate spikes >X in last 30s, temporarily bias keep-hot for 60s.
5) Add a burst detector that logs and emits an incident when: qps >= 4x baseline AND dram_read_bytes > baseline*1.5 for 5s. This triggers conservative fallback policies.

Medium-term engineering fixes / experiments to prioritize:
- KV residency-aware routing: route bursty traffic to lanes with reserved cache residency (dedicated pools) to avoid cross-tenant thrash.
- Hardware offload: investigate using NIC/GPU direct prefetch hooks where available to reduce CPU DMA stalls.
- Hybrid eviction policy: combine recency and inter-request reuse prediction using a lightweight ML model trained on per-route traces.
- Reinforced admission control: short-term queuing in front of serving runtime to smooth microbursts for small prompt workloads.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How frequent are pathological random-access bursts across customer mix? We have sample signals but need to quantify.
- Hot-key semantics: some model families have micro-hotspots by token; are our reuse heuristics pestering those keys?
- Cost of enabling NUMA pinning globally vs complexity of scheduling across heterogeneous fleets.

Action items (owner tags):
- @Aisha: add a burst-detection metric to core telemetry pipeline and dashboard (INF-2143). Due: 2025-12-05.
- @Tomás: run full sweep comparing 4Ms vs 2Ms hugepage settings on staging (write script + results table). Due: 2025-12-02.
- @Riley: prototype eviction-hysteresis toggle and run load tests with spike profile. Due: 2025-12-09.
- @Anika: prepare customer-impact assessment for Dedicated pools and recommend default knobs. Due: 2025-12-12.

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Tried increasing KV cache size by 10% locally; helped but is not a long term solution (cost and memory limits).
- Consider adding small async pre-warm path when a route sees >3 sequential misses within 100ms. Could be a compromise between prefetch and waste.
- Remember to check GPU driver patch notes for reported DMA stalls in 515.x series.

References / links:
- Trace reproducer: github.com/redwood/trace-tools/blob/main/reproduce_trace.py
- Related incident log: link-internal/INC-2025-11-12-kv-burst
- Prior notes (longtail reuse): shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/long-tail-reuse-and-memory-channel-contention-notes.json

Appendix: quick commands
- start perf counters: sudo perf stat -e dram_read_bytes,LLC-load-misses -p $(pidof serving-runtime) -- sleep 20
- dump residency: curl -s localhost:9000/metrics | grep kv_residency
- run trace reproducer: python3 reproduce_trace.py --profile=spike12s.json --target localhost:8080 --concurrency 60

End of playbook.

(Working doc — expect iteration; will convert to runbook once we validate mitigations in staging.)
